mdx.body:
The UniversalFilter component gives every table, catalog, and list in Layer5 projects a consistent way to narrow down what is displayed. Instead of each view inventing its own filter bar, a single control renders one dropdown per filterable attribute, collects the user's choices, and commits them all at once.

Overview

 Use the UniversalFilter when a data set can be narrowed along two or more independent attributes — for example filtering designs by type and visibility, or connections by kind and status. The control appears as a filter icon with a badge showing how many attributes are currently constrained. Clicking it opens a panel containing one select per attribute and an Apply button. Selections are held as a draft while the panel is open and are only committed to the parent when Apply is pressed, so a user can adjust several attributes without triggering a re-fetch for each change. On screens narrower than the sm breakpoint the panel is presented as a bottom sheet instead of a popper, so the same component works on mobile without extra code.

Anatomy
  • Filter trigger — A tooltip icon button labelled "Filter" that opens and closes the panel.
  • Active filter badge — A primary-coloured badge over the trigger, counting the attributes whose value is set to something other than All. It is hidden when nothing is filtered.
  • Panel — A popper anchored to the trigger on desktop, or a bottom sheet titled "Filters" on small screens.
  • Filter groups — One label and select per entry in the filters schema, rendered in the order the keys are declared.
  • Date range section — Optional. A "Quick Ranges" select plus Start and End date-time pickers, rendered only when date filtering is enabled.
  • Apply button — Commits the draft selections, closes the panel, and invokes the apply handler.

Variants

Attribute filtering

The default form. Each key in the filters schema becomes a select with an All option prepended, letting the user clear an individual attribute without clearing the rest.

Filtering with date range

Setting datePicker adds a date-range section beneath the attribute selects. It offers preset ranges such as Last 7 days and Last 30 days, alongside explicit start and end pickers for arbitrary windows.

Input variants

The variant prop is forwarded to every select in the panel, so the filter can be rendered as outlined (default), filled, or standard to match the surrounding form styling.

Accessibility
  • The trigger is a tooltip icon button with the accessible name "Filter", so it is reachable and operable from the keyboard.
  • Every filter group renders a visible label bound to its select — always give each entry in the schema a human-readable name.
  • The badge count is supplementary information; the applied values remain visible inside the panel, so meaning is never carried by the badge alone.
  • The panel closes on click-away and returns focus to the page, and the bottom sheet variant provides its own dismiss affordance on touch devices.
  • Pass a unique id per instance so multiple filters on one page remain individually addressable by assistive technology and tests.
